blogs.title: Third Time’s a Charm: TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV after Treated Endocarditis—When Is It Reasonable?
blogs.description: A decision framework for transcatheter redo after prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE): what the 2025 ESC guidance says, what “infection control” really looks like (negative cultures, TEE/MSCT without vegetations or PVL), and how prohibitive surgical risk can shift the balance toward TAVI. Pearls on timing post-antibiotics, pitfalls of smoldering infection, and how prior PVE should inform—without automatically vetoing—redo TAVI once cure is established.

blogs.title: Reading the Neo‑Skirt: CT Planning to Dodge Coronary Obstruction in Triple TAVR
blogs.description: CT pearls for layered frames: measuring ostial height, sinus dimensions, valve‑to‑coronary distance, and anticipating the neo‑skirt. How high implantation to pin prior leaflets can preserve both coronary flow and access, when you can safely forgo coronary protection, and the common misreads that get you into trouble in TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV.

blogs.title: The Gradient That Vanished: Making Sense of Early Severe PPM after Redo TAVR
blogs.description: Why a post‑implant mean gradient of 67 mm Hg with low DVI can fall into the 20s within weeks. Mechanisms include initial under‑expansion, delayed self‑expander remodeling, post‑dilation effects, and LV afterload regression. Practical tips: use DVI and indexed AVA, avoid knee‑jerk reintervention, and choose supra‑annular platforms/implant depth to eke out effective orifice area in tight, layered anatomies.

blogs.title: Frame‑on‑Frame Strategy: Cross‑Platform Valve Choice and Commissural Alignment That Matter
blogs.description: Selecting an Acurate neo2 after Lotus→Evolut: supra‑annular leaflet position, frame height, and alignment features that help in cramped, triple‑stented spaces. How to perform CT‑guided commissural alignment across platforms, use fluoroscopic landmarks, and why alignment in redo cases is about more than elegance—it’s about hemodynamics and future coronary reaccess.

blogs.title: Coronary Access in a Steel Cage: Future PCI after Multiple TAVRs
blogs.description: Planning for tomorrow’s cath today: assessing mesh burden, commissural-to-ostium relationships, and sinotubular clearance to keep PCI feasible after serial TAVRs. Techniques for future access (catheter choices, wiring strategies), when to consider leaflet modification (BASILICA) or protection, and current evidence gaps in navigating triple‑frame coronaries.

blogs.title: When the Access Bites Back: Preventing and Managing Vascular Complications in Redo TAVR
blogs.description: From a prior femoral pseudoaneurysm to a clean third procedure: best practices for access in redo TAVR—CT iliofemoral sizing, ultrasound‑guided puncture, closure strategy, leveraging radial for ancillary catheters, and bailout plans for hematoma/pseudoaneurysm. Practical checkpoints to keep bleeding and limb ischemia off your complication list.
